statement: The NPI is a 10-position, intelligence-free numeric identifier, the unique identification number for covered health care providers; CMS directs users to NPPES for application and access.
inference: Project inference: the NPI identifies a provider role, not a patient, and is published through NPPES, so it is a public provider identifier rather than a patient-linked reference. Whether every NPI use is public was not checked.

notes: The page read does not state the check digit method or whether individual and organizational NPIs differ.
No NPPES public-access terms were read.

statement: The NPI check digit uses the Luhn formula (modulus 10) with the 80840 prefix; the document includes a worked example.
location: CMS NPI check digit PDF, title and table of contents
inference: Check-digit structure makes a bare 10-digit value shape checkable, which supports identity of an NPI but not that it is sensitive. The CMS worked example value is deliberately not copied here.

notes: Only the document title, table of contents and check-digit description were read in summary form.
Whether the CMS example is a real issued NPI was not established, so it is not used.

statement: HL7 v2 table 0203 defines NPI (national provider identifier), PRN (provider number), RPH (pharmacist license number), SL (state license), FI (facility ID), XX (organization identifier), PLAC (placer identifier), FILL (filler identifier), VN (visit number), AN (account number) and PI (patient internal identifier) as distinct identifier types.
location: HL7 v2 table 0203, codes NPI, PRN, RPH, SL, FI, XX, PLAC, FILL, VN, AN, PI
inference: Project inference: provider, pharmacist, facility and organization codes name non-patient roles; PLAC and FILL are order-system references, VN is an encounter reference and AN an account reference, each of which may be joined to a patient only through other data.

notes: No value format is stated for any of these codes.
Whether PLAC/FILL/VN/AN values are person-linked on their own is not source-stated.

statement: Practitioner.identifier is an identifier that applies to a person in a practitioner role; Encounter.identifier is an identifier by which an encounter is known, and Encounter.subject is the patient or group present; no value format is stated for either.
location: FHIR R4 Practitioner.identifier; Encounter.identifier and Encounter.subject
inference: Project inference: encounter references link to a patient through a separate element, the same structure as Claim.patient and MedicationRequest.subject; practitioner identifiers are role identifiers, not patient identifiers.

notes: Only part of the Encounter page (first 100000 characters) was read.
The Practitioner page was read in summary only.
